message: Thanks, I can help with that. To start, which state do you live in, and how many people live in your household, including you?

message: Thanks. A few more quick questions: is there a married couple in the household? Is any child under 5? About how much do you pay in rent or mortgage each month? And roughly how much is in bank accounts and investments?

message: Thanks. Could you tell me the ages of your two children (roughly is fine)? Also, do you rent, own, or neither? Does anyone get health insurance through a job? And just to confirm, do you have $0 in rent or mortgage, and under $2,000 in bank accounts?
reply: No idea, honestly. We own our house. No, we buy our own or go without. Zero. We don't have any of that.

message: Thanks, that helps. Last few questions: Is anyone pregnant, or is there a baby under 1? Is any child under 5? Is anyone 65 or older, or does anyone have a disability? Is anyone a full-time college student or self-employed?
reply: No, not us. No idea, honestly. No, not us. No, everyone's healthy. No, not us. I'd have to check.

message: One more, to be sure: is either child younger than 5 years old? And does anyone in the household work for themselves (freelance, contract, or small business), or is all your income from regular paychecks?
reply: No idea, honestly. I'd have to check.

summary: Household: Louisiana, 4 people (two married parents, two children), about $14,400/year from work (about $1,200/month), no employer health insurance, own their home, about $0 in savings, no one pregnant or under 1, no one 65+, no disabilities, no college students. Recommended now: SNAP (food), Medicaid (covers parents and children at this income; Louisiana expanded Medicaid), Earned Income Tax Credit, refundable Child Tax Credit (file a tax return to claim both), and free school meals for the children. Not recommended: ACA premium tax credit (income is below the level where Medicaid applies, so Medicaid is the right route) and CHIP (children at this income fall under Medicaid). SSI doesn't apply (no disability or age-65+ member). Open items for a caseworker: WIC depends on whether either child is under 5, which the family didn't know; and TANF (Louisiana cash aid) is strict on income and work requirements, so the caseworker should check it. Self-employment status was also unclear, which could change the EITC/CTC figures.
